payload.body: Harmonicity is a human-made audio analysis feature that quantifies how closely a signal's spectral content matches a periodic (harmonic) model versus a noise-like model. It is computed by comparing the energy of spectral peaks that align with a harmonic template (partials at integer multiples of a fundamental frequency f0) to the residual energy that falls between those partials. Parameters: (1) a fundamental frequency estimate f0, (2) the number of harmonic partials to consider, (3) a tolerance window around each partial bin, (4) the power spectrum from which energy is measured. The persistence mechanism is the ratio H = E_harmonic / (E_harmonic + E_residual), yielding a value in [0, 1], where 1 indicates perfect harmonicity and 0 indicates pure noise. payload.body: Spectral-band-asymmetry is a statistical descriptor quantifying how unevenly spectral energy is distributed across the frequency bins within a defined sub-band. Parameters: (1) lower and upper frequency bounds of the sub-band, (2) the energy values per frequency bin within the band. Computed as the normalized sum of absolute deviations from the band centroid: A = sum_i(|f_i - f_c| * E_i) / sum_i(E_i), where f_i is the frequency of bin i, f_c is the band centroid (weighted mean frequency), and E_i is the energy in bin i. The value is expressed in Hertz and indicates the spatial spread of energy around the centroid — higher values mean energy is concentrated toward one edge of the band, lower values mean energy is more centrally distributed. Persistence mechanism: arithmetic computation over the finite set of per-bin energy values for the given band and analysis frame. [formal: asymmetria spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: Spectral-peak-trough-ratio is a human-made spectral feature quantifying the contrast between dominant spectral peaks and the valleys between them within a defined frequency range. It is computed by first identifying local maxima (peaks) and minima (troughs) in the magnitude spectrum, then calculating the ratio of mean peak energy to mean trough energy: PTR = mean(E_peak) / mean(E_trough). Parameters: (1) a frequency range or band over which to compute the ratio, (2) a minimum peak height threshold to distinguish true peaks from noise, (3) a minimum distance between adjacent peaks. Values greater than 1 indicate a spectrum with prominent peaks above the trough floor; higher values indicate sharper, more tonal spectra. Persistence mechanism: computed numerically from discrete magnitude spectra, stored as a scalar value per analysis frame. [formal: ratio culminis et vallis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]
